questions.question: Several biological processes are catalysed by enzymes. Digestive enzymes are present in which part of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are small organelles found in eukaryotic cells, often referred to as the cell's **"digestive system."**
 
• They contain a variety of **digestive enzymes**, such as proteases, lipases, and nucleases, which help in breaking down macromolecules like **proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.**
 
• The digestive enzymes within lysosomes function optimally at an **acidic pH**, which is maintained by proton pumps located in the lysosomal membrane.
 
• The primary role of lysosomes is to **degrade cellular waste** and recycle cellular components through processes like **autophagy** (self-eating) and **endocytosis** (engulfing materials from outside the cell).
 
• The enzymes in lysosomes are synthesized in the **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER)** and are transported to lysosomes via the **Golgi apparatus.**
 
• **Lysosomal dysfunction** can lead to various diseases, such as **Tay-Sachs disease** and **Gaucher's disease**, which are caused by the accumulation of undigested substances.
 
• Lysosomes are often termed as **"suicidal bags"** of the cell because they release enzymes that can digest the cell itself when it is damaged or no longer functional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ribosome**__

 __
 
• **Ribosomes** are responsible for **protein synthesis** in the cell.
 
• They are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be found either **free-floating** in the cytoplasm or attached to the **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER).**
 
• Unlike lysosomes, ribosomes do not contain digestive enzymes.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Complex**__
 __
 
• The **Golgi complex** is responsible for **modifying, packaging, and transporting proteins and lipids.**
 
• It plays a crucial role in the formation of **lysosomes** by packaging enzymes into vesicles.
 
• It does not directly participate in digestion but aids in the transport of enzymes to lysosomes.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**__
 
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **"powerhouses"** of the cell.
 
• They are responsible for generating **ATP** (adenosine triphosphate) through the process of **cellular respiration.**
 
• They do not contain digestive enzymes and are not involved in cellular digestion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the Swaran Singh Committee?

options.text: The committee was established during Indira Gandhi's Government
The 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act was based on its recommendations.
It suggested nine items as duties of the citizens.
The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in 1976.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was set up in the year **1976** during the tenure of **Indira Gandhi's Government**.
 
• The committee was established to study the concept of **Fundamental Duties** and recommend their inclusion in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The recommendations of the committee were incorporated into the Constitution through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, 1976, which added a new part, **Part IV-A**, and introduced **Article 51A**.
 
• The committee suggested the inclusion of **Fundamental Duties**, but it proposed **eight duties**, not nine as stated in the incorrect option.
 
• These Fundamental Duties were aimed at promoting a sense of **patriotism** and strengthening the spirit of **unity and integrity** in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**__

 __
 
• The **42nd Amendment**, also known as the **“Mini-Constitution”**, was passed in **1976** and brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the concept of **Fundamental Duties** to the Constitution under **Article 51A**.
 
• It also made changes to the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and extended the scope of the **Preamble** by adding the words **“Socialist,” “Secular,” and “Integrity.”**
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi’s Government**__
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi** served as the Prime Minister of India during the **Emergency period (1975–1977).**
 
• Her government introduced several constitutional changes, including the **42nd Amendment Act**.
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was one of the significant initiatives during her tenure to strengthen the values of **nationalism** and **responsibility** among citizens.

questions.question: Which ruler succeeded Chandragupta Maurya in 297 BCE?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara** was the second ruler of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• He succeeded his father, **Chandragupta Maurya**, in **297 BCE**.
 
• Bindusara was known by the title **Amitraghata**, which means "**Slayer of Enemies**".
 
• His reign was marked by the consolidation of the Mauryan empire, which was already expanded under Chandragupta.
 
• Bindusara maintained friendly relations with the **Hellenistic kingdoms** and received ambassadors like **Dionysius** from Egypt.
 
• He ruled for approximately **25 years** and was succeeded by his son, **Ashoka the Great**.
 
• Bindusara expanded the empire further into the **Deccan region**, excluding areas like Kalinga.
 
• Historical texts like the **Mahavamsa** and writings of **Greek historians** provide insights into his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kumaragupta**__

 __
 
• **Kumaragupta** was a ruler of the **Gupta Empire**, not the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He ruled in the 5th century CE and is known for founding the **Nalanda University**.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Gupta Empire's prosperity and cultural achievements.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 __
 
• **Ashoka**, also known as **Ashoka the Great**, was the son of Bindusara and succeeded him as the Mauryan ruler.
 
• He is renowned for his role in spreading **Buddhism** across Asia after the **Kalinga War**.
 
• Ashoka's reign marked one of the most celebrated eras in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Kanishka**__
 
 
• **Kanishka** was a ruler of the **Kushan Empire**, not related to the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• He is famous for his contributions to **Buddhism** and initiating the **Kanishka Era** in 78 CE.
 
• Kanishka's reign witnessed the spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and China.

• **Kerala's high sex ratio** reflects its focus on social welfare, education, and healthcare, which contribute to a better position for women.
 
• The state has also been a leader in achieving higher levels of **literacy and gender equality**, which positively impact the sex ratio.

 __

• The state's sex ratio is close to the national average but lower than states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Andhra Pradesh has implemented several social welfare programs, but challenges such as gender-based disparity still exist.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**__
 __
 
• **Karnataka** recorded a sex ratio of **973 females per 1000 males** according to the Census 2011.

• Efforts to improve gender equality are being undertaken in the state.

questions.question: In 2023, the Government of India proposed 'Amrit Dharohar Scheme' to be implemented over the next ____________ to encourage optimal use of wetlands and enhance bio-diversity, carbon stock, ecotourism opportunities and income generation for local communities.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Three Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Amrit Dharohar Scheme** was proposed by the **Government of India** in **2023**.
 
• It is designed to be implemented over the next **three years** to achieve sustainable management of **wetlands in India**.
 
• The scheme aims to encourage the **optimal use of wetlands**, which are crucial ecosystems for biodiversity and climate resilience.
 
• It seeks to enhance **biodiversity, carbon stock**, and **ecotourism opportunities**, while also generating income for **local communities**.
 
• **Wetlands** play a critical role in maintaining ecological balance by acting as **natural water purifiers**, mitigating **floods**, and serving as **carbon sinks**.
 
• The scheme aligns with India’s commitment to environmental goals under global frameworks like the **Ramsar Convention** and the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The initiative emphasizes the involvement of **local communities** in the sustainable management of wetlands, ensuring their active participation in conservation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wetlands and their Importance**__

 __
 
• **Wetlands** are ecosystems where water covers the soil or is present at or near the surface for varying periods of time.
 
• They are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for various species of **flora and fauna**.
 
• Wetlands are critical for **climate change mitigation** as they act as significant **carbon sinks**.
 
• They also support livelihoods by offering opportunities for **fishing, farming, and tourism**.
 
 
 
• **Ramsar Convention**__
 
 
• The **Ramsar Convention** is an international treaty signed in **1971** for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.
 
• India is a signatory to this convention and has a total of **75 Ramsar sites** as of 2023.
 
• The Ramsar sites in India include **Sundarbans, Chilika Lake, Loktak Lake, and Keoladeo National Park**.

questions.question: 0.26 g of an organic compound gave 0.13 g of water after complete combustion. The percentage composition of hydrogen is ________
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.0578**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem involves calculating the **percentage composition of hydrogen** in an organic compound based on the given data.
 
• To determine the hydrogen percentage, we use the following formula: **(Mass of hydrogen / Mass of the organic compound) × 100**.
 
• In the given problem, the mass of water produced is **0.13 g**.
 
• Water (H₂O) contains **2 parts of hydrogen** by weight and **16 parts of oxygen** by weight. Thus, the ratio of hydrogen in water is **2/18 = 1/9**.
 
• From the mass of water, the mass of hydrogen can be calculated as: **(1/9) × 0.13 g = 0.01444 g**.
 
• The mass of the organic compound is given as **0.26 g**.
 
• Now, the percentage of hydrogen is calculated as: **(0.01444 g / 0.26 g) × 100 = 5.78% or 0.0578**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **0.0578**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Concept:** The calculation of hydrogen percentage is based on the principle of **elemental analysis**, which is widely used in chemistry to determine the composition of compounds.
 
• **Water as a Product:** The combustion of organic compounds typically produces **water and carbon dioxide**, helping chemists analyze the hydrogen and carbon content.
 
• **Hydrogen in Water:** The ratio of hydrogen in water (1/9) is critical in such calculations. This ratio originates from the molecular weight of **H₂O** (18) and the atomic weight of hydrogen (2).

• The palace features intricate carvings, expansive halls, and terraces, along with water channels that enhanced its aesthetic appeal.
 
• Jahaz Mahal is a popular tourist destination and an important historical site that reflects the grandeur of the **Malwa Sultanate.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the Sultan of Delhi when Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 CE?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Muhammad bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was the Sultan of Delhi from **1325 CE to 1351 CE**.
 
• He was a ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and succeeded his father, **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.
 
• During his reign, the **Bahmani Kingdom** was established in 1347 CE in the **Deccan region** by **Alauddin Bahman Shah**, marking the beginning of an independent Muslim state in South India.
 
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq is known for his ambitious and often controversial policies, including the shifting of his capital from **Delhi to Daulatabad** and introducing token currency.
 
• His reign was marked by administrative reforms, but many of them failed due to **poor implementation**.
 
• He faced several revolts during his rule, including the revolt that led to the establishment of the **Bahmani Kingdom**.
 
• Despite his failures, Muhammad bin Tughlaq is remembered as a ruler with **visionary ideas**, albeit ahead of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mubarak Shah Khalji**__

 __
 
• **Mubarak Shah Khalji** was a ruler of the **Khalji dynasty** and reigned from **1316 to 1320 CE**.
 
• He was the last ruler of the Khalji dynasty before the establishment of the **Tughlaq dynasty.**
 
• His reign was marked by internal strife and instability, which ultimately led to his assassination.
 
 
 
• **Bahlul Lodi**__
 __
 
• **Bahlul Lodi** was the founder of the **Lodi dynasty**, which succeeded the Tughlaq dynasty in **1451 CE**.
 
• He ruled Delhi as Sultan and worked to consolidate his authority over North India.
 
• The Lodi dynasty marked the last phase of the Delhi Sultanate before the advent of the **Mughal Empire.**
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**__
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was the founder of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and ruled from **1320 CE to 1325 CE.**
 
• He is remembered for his administrative reforms and attempts to stabilize the Sultanate after the turbulent reign of the Khalji dynasty.
 
• His reign saw the construction of the **Tughlaqabad Fort** in Delhi.

questions.question: In which of the following cities of India was the first successful textile mill established?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first successful **textile mill** in India was established in **Mumbai** in the year **1854**.
 
• Mumbai emerged as the ideal location for the establishment of the textile mill due to its proximity to the **cotton-growing areas** in western India, particularly in Maharashtra.
 
• The availability of a **port** in Mumbai facilitated the import of machinery and export of finished goods, making it a strategic location for textile production.
 
• The mill was founded by a **Parsee entrepreneur**, Cowasji Nanabhai Davar, and was called the **Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company**.
 
• Mumbai became known as the **Manchester of India** due to its dominance in the textile industry during the British era.
 
• The establishment of the first textile mill marked the beginning of the **industrial revolution** in India and set the stage for the growth of the textile industry across the country.
 
• The textile industry in Mumbai played a significant role in boosting employment and contributing to the **economic development** of the region.
 
• It laid the foundation for **modern industries** in India and encouraged other industrial activities in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chennai**__

 __
 
• **Chennai**, also known as Madras, is an important industrial hub in southern India but was not the location for the first successful textile mill.
 
• It is known for its **automobile and software industries**, as well as traditional industries like leather and textiles.
 
• Chennai has a rich history of cotton textile production, but its prominence came later compared to Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Lucknow**__
 __
 
• **Lucknow**, the capital city of Uttar Pradesh, is renowned for its traditional **Chikankari embroidery**, which is a hand-embroidery technique.
 
• It is not historically associated with the establishment of large-scale textile mills during the industrial revolution era.
 
• Lucknow's contributions to textiles are more focused on traditional crafts rather than modern textile mills.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata**__
 
 
• **Kolkata**, formerly known as Calcutta, was an important commercial center during British rule but was not the site of the first textile mill.
 
• The city is known for its **jute industry**, with the first jute mill established in the late 19th century.
 
• Kolkata has a long history of industrial activity but was more prominent in industries like jute and tea rather than cotton textiles during the initial stages of industrialization in India.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was provided for the establishment of a federal court in India?

options.text: The Government of India Act of 1935
The Government of India Act of 1919

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Government of India Act of 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act of 1935** was a landmark legislation introduced by the British Parliament.
 
• This Act provided for the establishment of a **Federal Court in India**, which began functioning in **1937.**
 
• The Federal Court was established to resolve disputes between the **central government** and the **provincial governments** and to hear appeals from High Courts.
 
• The Federal Court served as a precursor to the **Supreme Court of India**, which was established post-independence in **1950.**
 
• It had original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, bringing a new judicial structure to India.
 
• The Act also proposed the creation of an All-India Federation consisting of **British Indian provinces** and **princely states**.
 
• This legislation introduced significant reforms, including the introduction of provincial autonomy and the separation of powers between the **executive** and the **judiciary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Regulating Act of 1773**__

 __
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a **Governor-General of Bengal** and a Supreme Court in Calcutta but did not provide for a Federal Court.
 
• Its main aim was to curb corruption and mismanagement within the East India Company.
 
 
 
• **The Indian Councils Act of 1909**__
 __
 
• Also known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, this Act introduced reforms in the legislative councils.
 
• It allowed for the inclusion of **Indians** in legislative councils but did not address the judiciary or provide for a Federal Court.
 
• This Act aimed to increase Indian representation in governance rather than judicial reforms.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1919**__
 
 
• This Act, also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, introduced the concept of **dyarchy** in provincial governments.
 
• It focused more on **administrative reforms** and provincial autonomy and did not provide for the establishment of a Federal Court.
 
• Its primary objective was to prepare Indians for gradual self-governance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the national income?

options.text: Income received by a person as a donation
Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill
Income received by a person for the use of his capital
Income received by a household for the use of their land

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Income received by a person as a donation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Income received by a person as a donation** is excluded from the **national income** because it does not represent any productive activity or contribution to the economy.
 
• National income is calculated based on the value of goods and services produced within a country during a specific time period, and donations are considered **voluntary transfers** rather than income earned through economic activities.
 
• Donations are typically categorized as **unilateral transfers**, which include gifts, grants, or aid, and do not reflect the country's economic productivity.
 
• Examples of unilateral transfers include **charitable contributions, foreign aid, and remittances**. These are excluded because they are not tied to the production of goods or services.
 
• The exclusion of donations ensures that the national income reflects only **, thereby accurately measuring the country's economic performance.
 
• This distinction is crucial in economic analysis to differentiate between earned income** and transfers that do not result from productive activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill**__

 __
 
• This income is included in the national income as it represents **payment for services** related to entrepreneurship, such as managing businesses, organizing production, or innovating.
 
• It is considered part of the **factor income** earned through productive activity and contributes to the economy.
 
• Entrepreneurial income falls under the category of **profit**, which is a key component of national income calculation.
 
 
 
• **Income received by a person for the use of his capital**__
 __
 
• This income represents **interest payments** or returns on investments and is included in the national income because it is a reward for the productive use of capital.
 
• Capital income contributes to the economic output and reflects the **monetary value of resources** used in production.
 
 
 
• **Income received by a household for the use of their land**__
 
 
• This income is categorized as **rent**, which is included in national income as it represents payment for the use of a productive resource.
 
• Land is a factor of production, and the income derived from its use is considered part of the economic activity that contributes to the national income.

questions.question: Jon Beel mela is held every year in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jon Beel Mela** is an annual event held in the state of **Assam**, India.
 
• This unique fair is conducted in the **Morigaon district** of Assam and is one of the oldest fairs in the region.
 
• The fair primarily celebrates the traditional system of **barter trade**, where goods are exchanged without the use of money.
 
• It is organized by the **Tiwa community**, an indigenous tribe in Assam, and holds cultural significance for them.
 
• The fair spans over three days and attracts participants not only from Assam but also from neighboring states and regions.
 
• Various items such as **agricultural products, food items, and handicrafts** are exchanged through the barter system during the fair.
 
• The fair also includes **traditional dances, music, and rituals**, showcasing the rich heritage of the Tiwa community.
 
• It serves as a platform for fostering **cultural exchange** and building community ties among different groups.
 
• The name "Jon Beel" comes from the **Jon Beel wetland**, which is located near the site of the fair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haryana**__

 __
 
• **Haryana** is primarily known for its rich agricultural output and sports culture.
 
• It is home to several fairs and festivals, such as the **Surajkund Mela**, which showcases handicrafts and cultural artifacts.
 
• The state does not host the **Jon Beel Mela**, as the fair is specific to the Tiwa community of Assam.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**__
 __
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** is known for its indigenous tribes and vibrant cultural festivals, such as the **Losar Festival** and **Nyokum Festival**.
 
• Though it has several fairs, the **Jon Beel Mela** is not held in this state.
 
 
 
• **Telangana**__
 
 
• **Telangana** is known for events like the **Bathukamma Festival** and **Kakatiya Festival**, which reflect its regional identity.
 
• The state does not host the **Jon Beel Mela**, as it is specific to Assam.

questions.question: Proposed in 2023-24, which section of the Income Tax Act of 1961 exempts senior citizens aged 75 years and above from filing income tax returns?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Section 194P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 194P** was introduced in the **Finance Act 2021** and became applicable from **1st April 2021**.
 
• This section provides relief to **senior citizens aged 75 years and above**, exempting them from filing income tax returns under certain conditions.
 
• The exemption applies only if the senior citizen has income exclusively from **pension and interest** earned on deposits in the same bank where the pension is credited.
 
• The bank, in such cases, is required to deduct the applicable **tax at source (TDS)** after considering deductions under **Chapter VI-A** like **Section 80C, 80D, etc.**, ensuring no tax liability remains.
 
• This provision aims to simplify tax compliance for elderly individuals who might face challenges in filing returns due to **age or health-related reasons**.
 
• It is applicable only for banks that have been notified by the government for this purpose, ensuring proper implementation.
 
• Senior citizens must submit a declaration to the bank confirming their eligibility under this section.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Section 139A**__

 __
 
• **Section 139A** of the Income Tax Act deals with the requirement of obtaining a **PAN (Permanent Account Number).**
 
• PAN is mandatory for certain transactions such as opening a bank account, filing income tax returns, and making financial transactions above a specific limit.
 
• This section helps in identifying taxpayers and linking their financial transactions.
 
 
 
• **Section 234C**__
 __
 
• **Section 234C** pertains to the payment of **interest for default or delay in payment of advance tax.**
 
• If a taxpayer fails to pay advance tax installments as required, interest is levied under this section.
 
• It ensures timely payment of taxes by taxpayers and prevents accumulation of tax liability.
 
 
 
• **Section 80C**__
 
 
• **Section 80C** allows taxpayers to claim deductions up to **₹1.5 lakh** for specified investments and expenses.
 
• Eligible investments include **PPF, ELSS, NSC, FD (5 years), etc.**
 
• This section encourages savings and investments by offering tax benefits.
